2357def _schema_key(schema: dict | None) -> tuple | None: 

2358 """Hashable, stable representation of a column-mapping schema dict. 

2359 

2360 Values may be strings, ``None``, or a list of column names (composite trial 

2361 id). Used as part of the normalization cache key so an override that changes 

2362 the mapping (without changing the raw frame) correctly busts the cache. 

2363 """ 

2364 if schema is None: 

2365 return None 

2366 return tuple( 

2367 (k, tuple(v) if isinstance(v, list) else v) for k, v in sorted(schema.items()) 

2368 ) 

2369 

2370 

2371@st.cache_data(show_spinner="Normalizing data…") 

2372def _normalize_pair_cached( 

2373 _words_df: pd.DataFrame, 

2374 _word_schema: dict | None, 

2375 _fixations_df: pd.DataFrame, 

2376 _fix_schema: dict | None, 

2377 cache_key, 

2378 _keep_words: set | None = None, 

2379 _keep_fix: set | None = None, 

2380) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: 

2381 """Pure normalize + harmonize, cached on a cheap fingerprint of the inputs. 

2382 

2383 The raw frames are passed un-hashed (underscore args); ``cache_key`` carries 

2384 a ``frame_fingerprint`` + schema signature + the keep-column selection 

2385 instead, so a trial change (which re-runs the script but feeds byte-identical 

2386 raw frames) hits the cache and skips re-normalizing the whole corpus, while 

2387 changing the kept columns correctly busts it. 

2388 """ 

2389 # UX-37: logged because a cache *miss* is exactly what a "why was that slow?" 

2390 # question is about, and a hit is silent — the line only appears when the 

2391 # work actually ran. 

2392 with timed( 

2393 "normalize + harmonize (cache miss)", 

2394 word_rows=len(_words_df), 

2395 fixation_rows=len(_fixations_df), 

2396 ): 

2397 words_norm = ( 

2398 normalize_words(_words_df, _word_schema, keep_columns=_keep_words) 

2399 if _word_schema is not None 

2400 else empty_words_frame() 

2401 ) 

2402 fixations_norm = ( 

2403 normalize_fixations(_fixations_df, _fix_schema, keep_columns=_keep_fix) 

2404 if _fix_schema is not None 

2405 else empty_fixations_frame() 

2406 ) 

2407 return harmonize_frames(words_norm, fixations_norm) 

2408 

2409 

2410def _normalize_pair( 

2411 words_df: pd.DataFrame, 

2412 word_schema: dict | None, 

2413 fixations_df: pd.DataFrame, 

2414 fix_schema: dict | None, 

2415 keep_words: set | None = None, 

2416 keep_fix: set | None = None, 

2417) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame]: 

2418 """Normalize a *validated* (words, fixations) pair to canonical columns and 

2419 run the cross-frame fixups (``harmonize_frames``). 

2420 

2421 A ``None`` schema means that table is absent (single-report dataset) → a 

2422 canonical empty frame. Records the composite-trial component columns (when 

2423 the trial id is built from several columns) so the trial picker can offer one 

2424 cascading selector per component. Shared by the upload and non-upload paths. 

2425 

2426 The heavy normalization is delegated to the cached ``_normalize_pair_cached`` 

2427 so it doesn't re-run on every rerun (e.g. selecting a different trial); only 

2428 the lightweight session-state bookkeeping below runs each time. 

2429 """ 

2430 trial_mapping = (word_schema or fix_schema)["trial"] 

2431 trial_cols = trial_mapping_columns(trial_mapping) 

2432 st.session_state["_composite_trial_columns"] = ( 

2433 trial_cols if len(trial_cols) > 1 else None 

2434 ) 

2435 cache_key = ( 

2436 frame_fingerprint(words_df), 

2437 _schema_key(word_schema), 

2438 frame_fingerprint(fixations_df), 

2439 _schema_key(fix_schema), 

2440 tuple(sorted(keep_words)) if keep_words is not None else None, 

2441 tuple(sorted(keep_fix)) if keep_fix is not None else None, 

2442 ) 

2443 return _normalize_pair_cached( 

2444 words_df, 

2445 word_schema, 

2446 fixations_df, 

2447 fix_schema, 

2448 cache_key, 

2449 _keep_words=keep_words, 

2450 _keep_fix=keep_fix, 

2451 ) 

2452 

2453 

2454def _reset_active_mapping() -> None: 

2455 """Clear the stashed column mapping at the start of each data load, so a new 

2456 source doesn't inherit the previous one's mapping in the Data Inspection tab.""" 

2457 st.session_state["_active_column_mapping"] = {} 

2458 

2459 

2460def _stash_active_mapping(table: str, schema: dict | None) -> None: 

2461 """Record the schema (field → source column) actually used for ``table`` so 

2462 ``tabs.render_data_inspection_tab`` can show how columns were mapped. ``table`` 

2463 is one of ``"words" / "fixations" / "raw_gaze"``.""" 

2464 mapping = st.session_state.setdefault("_active_column_mapping", {}) 

2465 mapping[table] = dict(schema) if schema else None 

2466 

2467 

2468#: Lead of the ``problems`` entry a **rejected** mapping produces, as opposed to 

2469#: an **incomplete** one. ``_render_unmapped_view`` branches on it to say the 

2470#: right thing, so keep the two in step. 

2471MAPPING_FAILURE_LEAD = "This column mapping doesn't work with this data" 

2472 

2473 

2474def mapping_failure_problem(exc: Exception) -> str: 

2475 """Turn a normalization failure into one more recovery ``problems`` entry. 

2476 

2477 Everything the normalize → harmonize pipeline raises is a statement about 

2478 the column mapping in force — a ``multipart`` identity rule (screen id in 

2479 only one report, orphan screens, a conflicting canvas), a non-numeric 

2480 coordinate column, a duplicated trial key. None of them is a reason to stop 

2481 rendering, and letting one propagate is actively a trap: the panels that 

2482 would fix the mapping are written *during* the run that dies, and the Data 

2483 page they live on is hidden while another view is active — so the user is 

2484 left with a traceback and nothing to click, which is how the app used to 

2485 wedge on a mapping it had auto-detected itself. 

2486 

2487 The exception is logged with its traceback (🐛 Debug panel + terminal) and 

2488 handed back as a string, so the existing incomplete-mapping recovery path — 

2489 raw tables, still-editable mapping panels, off-page signpost — carries it. 

2490 """ 

2491 logging.getLogger("scanpath_studio").exception( 

2492 "Normalizing with the current column mapping failed." 

2493 ) 

2494 return f"{MAPPING_FAILURE_LEAD}: {exc}" 

2495 

2496 

2497def reset_column_mapping() -> None: 

2498 """Drop every ``col_map_*`` key, so the mapping falls back to auto-detection. 

2499 

2500 Used both when the monitor-defining source changes (a mapping is keyed to 

2501 the columns it was made for) and as the escape hatch under a rejected 

2502 mapping. Safe from an ``on_click`` callback: it runs before the script that 

2503 re-creates the widgets. 

2504 """ 

2505 for key in [ 

2506 k 

2507 for k in list(st.session_state) 

2508 if isinstance(k, str) and k.startswith(COLUMN_MAPPING_PREFIX) 

2509 ]: 

2510 del st.session_state[key] 

2511 

2512 

2513#: Label + tooltip of the "known-good state" button, shared by the off-page 

2514#: signpost and the 💾 Session menu so the two read as the same action. 

2515DEMO_RESET_LABEL = "🧪 Load the bundled demo" 

2516DEMO_RESET_HELP = ( 

2517 "Switches to the demo corpus and re-detects its column mapping. Your " 

2518 "uploaded datasets stay in the source list." 

2519) 

2520 

2521 

2522def load_bundled_demo() -> None: 

2523 """``on_click``: return to the bundled demo with a freshly detected mapping. 

2524 

2525 The one button that reaches a known-good state from anywhere, for a session 

2526 wedged on a dataset it cannot normalize. Three things together, because any 

2527 two of them leave a way to stay stuck: the source switch (through the 

2528 pre-widget ``_pending_source_choice`` seam — assigning the picker's value 

2529 inline is reconciled away by the browser), leaving the wizard the way its 

2530 own ✕ Cancel does, and dropping the column mapping — which a source *change* 

2531 already does, but the wedged source is often the demo itself, and then 

2532 nothing would change without this. 

2533 """ 

2534 st.session_state["_pending_source_choice"] = DEMO_CHOICE 

2535 st.session_state["_show_upload_wizard"] = False 

2536 st.session_state["setup_complete"] = True 

2537 st.session_state.pop(WIZARD_LEAVE_KEY, None) 

2538 st.session_state.pop(WIZARD_STAY_KEY, None) 

2539 reset_column_mapping() 

2540 

2541 

2542def clear_computation_cache() -> None: 

2543 """``on_click``: drop every ``@st.cache_data`` entry for this process. 

2544 

2545 Used after deleting a dataset so derived values cannot retain its frames. 

2546 It does not touch the recovery cache or live session state, except for 

2547 DATA-32's remembered dataset counts, which are derived too. 

2548 """

2550 forget_dataset_counts()

2553def _apply_declared_schema(proposed: dict, declared: dict | None) -> dict: 

2554 """Auto-detection, overridden by whatever the source *declares* it knows. 

2555 

2556 Auto-detection guesses a mapping from column names, which is right for an 

2557 upload and wrong for a corpus whose schema is a published contract. The 

2558 declared mapping wins for every field it names — including a field it names 

2559 as ``None``, which is a positive statement that the source has no such 

2560 column and is what clears a leftover the detector would otherwise seize on. 

2561 Fields the source says nothing about keep their detected value, so optional 

2562 passthroughs (linguistic features, EyeLink measures) still arrive. 

2563 """ 

2564 if not declared: 

2565 return proposed 

2566 return {**proposed, **declared} 

2567 

2568 

2569def declared_schemas_for(data_choice: str) -> tuple[dict | None, dict | None]: 

2570 """The ``(word, fix)`` schemas the selected source publishes, or ``(None, None)``. 

2571 

2572 A prepared benchmark corpus has a **known** schema — the prep script wrote 

2573 it — and every other surface already loads one through it 

2574 (`eyegenbench.load_eyegenbench`, so `render --eyegenbench`, the headless API 

2575 and Comparisons' dataset B all agree). The app was the one surface that 

2576 re-guessed instead, and the guess is wrong on real bundles: the prepared 

2577 frames carry the publisher's ~190 leftover columns through, so EMTeC's 

2578 fixations detect `trial="TRIAL_ID"` against the words' `unique_paragraph_id` 

2579 and broadcast **zero** word boxes — silently, since only the words frame 

2580 ends up empty and the empty-pool guard never fires. 

2581 """ 

2582 if data_choice != PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE: 

2583 return None, None 

2584 spec = public_dataset_registry().get( 

2585 st.session_state.get("public_dataset_choice", "") 

2586 ) 

2587 if not spec or not spec.get("benchmark_dataset"): 

2588 return None, None 

2589 from scanpath_studio.eyegenbench import ( 

2590 EYEGENBENCH_FIX_SCHEMA, 

2591 EYEGENBENCH_WORD_SCHEMA, 

2592 ) 

2593 

2594 return dict(EYEGENBENCH_WORD_SCHEMA), dict(EYEGENBENCH_FIX_SCHEMA) 

2595 

2596 

2597def prepare_data( 

2598 words_df: pd.DataFrame, 

2599 fixations_df: pd.DataFrame, 

2600 allow_override: bool, 

2601 mapping_host=None, 

2602 declared_word_schema: dict | None = None, 

2603 declared_fix_schema: dict | None = None, 

2604) -> tuple[pd.DataFrame, pd.DataFrame, list]: 

2605 """Infer schemas and normalize incoming dataframes to canonical column names. 

2606 

2607 When ``allow_override`` is True, render sidebar expanders that let the user 

2608 pick the exact column names for each field (pre-filled with auto-detection). 

2609 Otherwise just auto-detect. 

2610 

2611 Returns ``(words_norm, fixations_norm, problems)``. ``problems`` is a list 

2612 of human-readable strings; when it's non-empty the column mapping isn't 

2613 usable yet (a required field is unmapped) — the normalized frames come back 

2614 empty and the caller shows the raw uploaded data so the user can pick the 

2615 right columns instead of the whole app halting (which used to hide the very 

2616 data needed to decide the mapping). 

2617 

2618 Either frame may arrive empty (single-report datasets: only an IA report, 

2619 or only a fixation report) — the missing side becomes a canonical empty 

2620 frame and its mapping UI is skipped. Cross-frame fixups (stimulus-level 

2621 words broadcast across participants, AOI-only fixations placed at word-box 

2622 centers) run at the end via ``harmonize_frames``. 

2623 """ 

2624 has_words = not words_df.empty 

2625 has_fixations = not fixations_df.empty 

2626 word_schema = None 

2627 fix_schema = None 

2628 problems: list = [] 

2629 

2630 if has_words: 

2631 word_proposed = _apply_declared_schema( 

2632 propose_word_schema(words_df), declared_word_schema 

2633 ) 

2634 if allow_override: 

2635 word_schema = column_mapping_ui( 

2636 words_df, 

2637 table_label="Words/IA", 

2638 state_key_prefix="col_map_words", 

2639 field_specs=WORD_FIELD_SPECS, 

2640 proposed=word_proposed, 

2641 problems=validate_word_schema(word_proposed), 

2642 container=mapping_host, 

2643 # The host is the ⚙️ Configure menu popover, which nests no 

2644 # expander — render the panel inline with its own bold header. 

2645 use_expander=False, 

2646 # Match the add-dataset screen's compact field grid instead of 

2647 # stretching every mapping across a full row. 

2648 columns_per_row=4, 

2649 stack_labels=True, 

2650 ) 

2651 else: 

2652 word_schema = word_proposed 

2653 word_problems = validate_word_schema(word_schema) 

2654 if word_problems: 

2655 problems.append("Words/IA: " + "; ".join(word_problems)) 

2656 

2657 if has_fixations: 

2658 fix_proposed = _apply_declared_schema( 

2659 propose_fix_schema(fixations_df), declared_fix_schema 

2660 ) 

2661 if allow_override: 

2662 fix_schema = column_mapping_ui( 

2663 fixations_df, 

2664 table_label="Fixations", 

2665 state_key_prefix="col_map_fix", 

2666 field_specs=FIX_FIELD_SPECS, 

2667 proposed=fix_proposed, 

2668 problems=validate_fix_schema(fix_proposed), 

2669 container=mapping_host, 

2670 use_expander=False, 

2671 columns_per_row=4, 

2672 stack_labels=True, 

2673 ) 

2674 else: 

2675 fix_schema = fix_proposed 

2676 fix_problems = validate_fix_schema(fix_schema) 

2677 if fix_problems: 

2678 problems.append("Fixations: " + "; ".join(fix_problems)) 

2679 

2680 if problems: 

2681 # Mapping not ready — let the caller surface the raw data instead of 

2682 # plotting. Clear any stale composite-trial state so the picker doesn't 

2683 # reference columns from a previous, valid dataset. 

2684 st.session_state["_composite_trial_columns"] = None 

2685 return empty_words_frame(), empty_fixations_frame(), problems 

2686 

2687 # Record the mapping actually used so the Data Inspection tab can show it. 

2688 _stash_active_mapping("words", word_schema if has_words else None) 

2689 _stash_active_mapping("fixations", fix_schema if has_fixations else None) 

2690 

2691 try: 

2692 words_norm, fixations_norm = _normalize_pair( 

2693 words_df, word_schema, fixations_df, fix_schema 

2694 ) 

2695 except Exception as exc: 

2696 # A mapping the pipeline *rejects* recovers the same way as one that is 

2697 # merely incomplete. See `mapping_failure_problem`. 

2698 st.session_state["_composite_trial_columns"] = None 

2699 return ( 

2700 empty_words_frame(), 

2701 empty_fixations_frame(), 

2702 [mapping_failure_problem(exc)], 

2703 ) 

2704 return words_norm, fixations_norm, problems 

2705 

2706 

2707# Labels of the top-level tab strip, shared by the real tabs, the 

2708# unmapped-data placeholder view, and the tab-persistence script so they can't 

2709# drift apart. 

2710# Bulk export is no longer a top-level tab — it's folded into the Scanpath 

2711# Visualization tab's "Export" subtab (see tabs._render_export_panel). 

2712# The two top-level views. Scanpath is the default page; Corpus Analysis is 

2713# reached via the header button (``_render_about_panel``). Data Inspection and 

2714# Share are now subtabs of the Scanpath view (tabs.render_single_trial_tab), 

2715# not standalone views. ``main_nav`` (session state) holds the active view. 

2716

2718def _render_raw_preview(label: str, df: pd.DataFrame) -> None: 

2719 """Show one uploaded table's columns + a sample so the user can map it.""" 

2720 if df is None or df.empty: 

2721 return 

2722 st.markdown(f"#### {label} — {len(df):,} rows × {df.shape[1]} columns") 

2723 st.caption("Columns: " + ", ".join(str(c) for c in df.columns)) 

2724 st.dataframe(df.head(200), width="stretch", height=320)

2727def _render_unmapped_view( 

2728 raw_words_df: pd.DataFrame, 

2729 raw_fixations_df: pd.DataFrame, 

2730 problems: list, 

2731) -> None: 

2732 """Show the raw uploaded data while the column mapping isn't usable. 

2733 

2734 Two different failures land here, and they need different words. A mapping 

2735 that is **incomplete** asks the user to fill a field in; one the pipeline 

2736 **rejected** (``MAPPING_FAILURE_LEAD``) already names what is wrong with the 

2737 combination they have — so it gets the error, the reason, and a one-click 

2738 way back to the auto-detected mapping, for when the offending pick came from 

2739 a restored session and editing the panel field by field is a scavenger hunt. 

2740 

2741 Either way the uploaded tables (unmodified) are shown below, so the user can 

2742 inspect column names and values while choosing. 

2743 """ 

2744 rejected = [p for p in problems if p.startswith(MAPPING_FAILURE_LEAD)] 

2745 if rejected: 

2746 for problem in rejected: 

2747 st.error(problem, icon="🚫") 

2748 st.caption( 

2749 "Change the field it names in the **Column mapping** section above, " 

2750 "or start again from what auto-detection proposes." 

2751 ) 

2752 st.button( 

2753 "↩️ Reset to the auto-detected mapping", 

2754 key="reset_column_mapping", 

2755 on_click=reset_column_mapping, 

2756 ) 

2757 else: 

2758 st.warning( 

2759 "**Finish the column mapping to draw scanpaths.** Map the missing " 

2760 "field(s) in the **Column mapping** section above — the raw data is " 

2761 "shown below to help you choose. " 

2762 "Still needed:\n\n" + "\n".join(f"- {p}" for p in problems) 

2763 ) 

2764 if (raw_words_df is None or raw_words_df.empty) and ( 

2765 raw_fixations_df is None or raw_fixations_df.empty 

2766 ): 

2767 st.info("No data loaded yet.") 

2768 _render_raw_preview("Words / IA", raw_words_df) 

2769 _render_raw_preview("Fixations", raw_fixations_df) 

2770

2772@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False) 

2773def _cached_participant_ids(_words, _fixations, cache_key) -> list: 

2774 """Every reader id in the dataset (DATA-20), memoized per frame pair. 

2775 

2776 Underscore-prefixed frames + an explicit `frame_fingerprint` key, the house 

2777 convention: this is a `.unique()` over the *unfiltered* corpus, which is 

2778 hundreds of milliseconds on a full-size one. 

2779 """ 

2780 del cache_key 

2781 return metadata_mod.participant_ids(_words, _fixations)

2784def _refresh_participant_metadata(participants) -> None: 

2785 """Re-report an attached participant table against the loaded readers. 

2786 

2787 The table outlives a data-source switch (it is session state, like the 

2788 annotations), so the join it was validated against can go stale the moment 

2789 a different corpus loads. Recomputing the report — not the fields — keeps 

2790 "no row for these readers" honest without asking the user to re-upload. 

2791 """ 

2792 from scanpath_studio import metadata as md 

2793 

2794 attached = st.session_state.get(md.SESSION_KEY) 

2795 if attached is None: 

2796 return 

2797 st.session_state[md.SESSION_KEY] = md.rejoin(attached, participants)

2800def _render_offpage_setup_notice(data_view: bool) -> None: 

2801 """Point at the **Data** page when setup is unfinished and we're elsewhere. 

2802 

2803 DATA-26: an unfinished dataset (a wizard mid-flight, or a required column 

2804 still unmapped) leaves the analysis views with nothing to draw — `main` 

2805 returns before them, exactly as it did before the page existed. What it used 

2806 to leave behind was a blank screen; the setup UI now lives on a page that is 

2807 rendered but hidden, so say where it went and offer one click to get there. 

2808 

2809 Deliberately *not* a forced `switch_to_view`: bouncing the user back every 

2810 run would make the other two views unreachable until the mapping is fixed, 

2811 and that is a worse trap than an empty page with a signpost. 

2812 

2813 The second button is the way out that does **not** go through the page: 

2814 finishing the setup is the right answer when the dataset is nearly there, 

2815 but a dataset the pipeline rejects can leave the user with nothing to plot 

2816 and no appetite for the mapping — and the source picker itself lives on the 

2817 page they'd rather not visit. See :func:`load_bundled_demo`. 

2818 """ 

2819 if data_view: 

2820 return 

2821 st.info( 

2822 "**This dataset isn't set up yet**, so there's nothing to plot. " 

2823 "Finish it on the 🗂️ **Data** page — or start over from the demo.", 

2824 icon="🗂️", 

2825 ) 

2826 finish, demo = st.columns(2) 

2827 finish.button( 

2828 "🗂️ Go to Data setup", 

2829 on_click=_go_data, 

2830 type="primary", 

2831 width="stretch", 

2832 key="offpage_go_to_setup", 

2833 ) 

2834 demo.button( 

2835 DEMO_RESET_LABEL, 

2836 on_click=load_bundled_demo, 

2837 width="stretch", 

2838 key="offpage_load_demo", 

2839 help=DEMO_RESET_HELP, 

2840 ) 

2841 

2842 

2843# File types accepted by every upload box. ``zip`` covers single-member 

2844# archives wrapping any of the others (e.g. ``data.csv.zip``). 

2845_UPLOAD_TYPES = ["csv", "tsv", "parquet", "feather", "zip", "xlsx", "xls"]

2848def _uploaded_file_key(uploaded) -> tuple: 

2849 """Stable cache key for an uploaded file across reruns. 

2850 

2851 ``st.file_uploader`` keeps the same ``UploadedFile`` (and ``file_id``) for a 

2852 given upload until it's replaced, so keying on it lets us parse the file 

2853 *once* instead of on every rerun.""" 

2854 return ( 

2855 getattr(uploaded, "file_id", None), 

2856 getattr(uploaded, "name", None), 

2857 getattr(uploaded, "size", None), 

2858 )

2861@st.cache_data(show_spinner="Reading uploaded data…") 

2862def _read_uploaded_table_cached(_uploaded, file_key) -> pd.DataFrame: 

2863 try: 

2864 _uploaded.seek(0) 

2865 except Exception: 

2866 pass 

2867 return read_table(_uploaded) 

2868 

2869 

2870@st.cache_data(show_spinner="Reading uploaded data…") 

2871def _read_uploaded_tables_cached(_uploaded_list, file_keys) -> pd.DataFrame: 

2872 for f in _uploaded_list: 

2873 try: 

2874 f.seek(0) 

2875 except Exception: 

2876 pass 

2877 return read_tables(list(_uploaded_list))

2879 

2880def _read_uploaded_frame( 

2881 *, 

2882 uploader_label: str, 

2883 upload_help: str, 

2884 state_prefix: str, 

2885 multi: bool, 

2886 container=None, 

2887) -> pd.DataFrame: 

2888 """Render one upload box and return its (concatenated) frame. 

2889 

2890 Renders in the sidebar by default; pass ``container`` (the setup wizard's 

2891 main-area container) to render it there. Empty frame when nothing is 

2892 uploaded. The file parse is cached on the upload's identity (see 

2893 ``_uploaded_file_key``) so a large uploaded table is read once, not re-parsed 

2894 on every rerun. Isolated from the mapping render so tests can inject frames 

2895 without a real upload (AppTest can't drive ``st.file_uploader``).""" 

2896 host = container if container is not None else st.container() 

2897 uploaded = host.file_uploader( 

2898 uploader_label, 

2899 type=_UPLOAD_TYPES, 

2900 accept_multiple_files=multi, 

2901 key=f"{state_prefix}_upload", 

2902 help=upload_help, 

2903 ) 

2904 if not uploaded: 

2905 return pd.DataFrame() 

2906 # BUG-5: a large upload parses/normalizes into several in-memory copies that 

2907 # can OOM-kill the ~1 GB hosted demo (no traceback). Warn and require an 

2908 # explicit opt-in before parsing. 

2909 # 

2910 # DATA-22 review: only on the *hosted* demo. Running locally there is no such 

2911 # ceiling — the warning was pure noise, and the "Load it anyway" tick was a 

2912 # step between the user and their own data on their own machine. Same 

2913 # loopback test the wizard's "run locally" tip uses. 

2914 if upload_exceeds_limit(uploaded) and not is_loopback_url( 

2915 str(getattr(st.context, "url", "") or "") 

2916 ): 

2917 mb = uploaded_files_total_bytes(uploaded) / (1024 * 1024) 

2918 host.warning( 

2919 f"This upload is **{mb:.0f} MB**. On the hosted demo (~1 GB RAM), " 

2920 "parsing a corpus this large can exhaust memory and crash the app. " 

2921 "For big corpora, run locally (`pip install scanpath-studio`) or " 

2922 "upload a subset (e.g. a few participants)." 

2923 ) 

2924 if not host.checkbox( 

2925 "Load it anyway", 

2926 key=f"{state_prefix}_load_large", 

2927 help="Parse this large upload regardless. Safe on a local machine " 

2928 "with enough RAM; may crash the memory-limited hosted demo.", 

2929 ): 

2930 return pd.DataFrame() 

2931 if multi: 

2932 return _read_uploaded_tables_cached( 

2933 uploaded, tuple(_uploaded_file_key(f) for f in uploaded) 

2934 ) 

2935 return _read_uploaded_table_cached(uploaded, _uploaded_file_key(uploaded)) 

2936 

2937 

2938def load_raw_gaze_data(data_choice: str, *, host=None, notices=None) -> pd.DataFrame: 

2939 """Load and normalize optional raw gaze data (millisecond-level eye positions). 

2940 

2941 Raw gaze data provides finer temporal resolution than fixation-level data 

2942 and enables overlay visualizations showing continuous gaze paths. 

2943 

2944 Args: 

2945 data_choice: The selected data source (e.g. ``DEMO_CHOICE`` loads the 

2946 bundled sample gaze; other built-in sources have none). The Upload 

2947 source and stored datasets carry their own raw gaze, so ``main`` 

2948 doesn't call this for them. 

2949 host: Where the optional uploader + its column mapping render — the 

2950 *Data location* section of the 🗂️ Data page (DATA-26). 

2951 notices: Where the "raw gaze ignored" warnings render. Deliberately the 

2952 strip under the menu bar, not ``host``: a warning on a page the user 

2953 isn't looking at is invisible, which the always-visible sidebar 

2954 never was. 

2955 

2956 Returns: 

2957 Normalized raw gaze DataFrame with canonical columns, or empty DataFrame 

2958 if not available or schema inference fails 

2959 

2960 Canonical Columns (raw gaze): 

2961 participant_id, trial_id, x, y, timestamp_ms (optional: text) 

2962 

2963 UI Effects: 

2964 - Renders optional file uploader for "Upload csv tables" mode 

2965 - Shows warning if schema inference fails 

2966 - Shows info message if sample data unavailable 

2967 """ 

2968 raw_gaze_df = pd.DataFrame() 

2969 cfg = host if host is not None else st.container() 

2970 warn = notices if notices is not None else st.container() 

2971 

2972 if data_choice in (SYNTHETIC_CHOICE, PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE): 

2973 # Neither the synthetic trial nor the public corpora ship raw gaze; 

2974 # skip the uploader entirely. 

2975 return raw_gaze_df 

2976 

2977 if data_choice == DEMO_CHOICE: 

2978 raw_gaze_df = load_sample_raw_gaze() 

2979 if not raw_gaze_df.empty: 

2980 raw_gaze_schema = infer_raw_gaze_schema(raw_gaze_df) 

2981 if raw_gaze_schema: 

2982 _stash_active_mapping("raw_gaze", raw_gaze_schema) 

2983 raw_gaze_df = normalize_raw_gaze(raw_gaze_df, raw_gaze_schema) 

2984 else: 

2985 warn.warning("Could not infer raw gaze schema from sample data") 

2986 raw_gaze_df = pd.DataFrame() 

2987 else: 

2988 uploaded_raw_gaze = cfg.file_uploader( 

2989 "Raw gaze table (optional)", 

2990 type=["csv", "parquet", "feather", "zip"], 

2991 help="Optional: millisecond-level gaze with participant_id, trial_id, x, y.", 

2992 ) 

2993 if uploaded_raw_gaze: 

2994 raw_gaze_df = read_table(uploaded_raw_gaze) 

2995 proposed = propose_raw_gaze_schema(raw_gaze_df) 

2996 initial_problems = validate_raw_gaze_schema(proposed) 

2997 with cfg: 

2998 raw_gaze_schema = column_mapping_ui( 

2999 raw_gaze_df, 

3000 table_label="Raw gaze", 

3001 state_key_prefix="col_map_raw_gaze", 

3002 field_specs=RAW_GAZE_FIELD_SPECS, 

3003 proposed=proposed, 

3004 problems=initial_problems, 

3005 ) 

3006 problems = validate_raw_gaze_schema(raw_gaze_schema) 

3007 if problems: 

3008 warn.warning("Raw gaze ignored — " + "; ".join(problems)) 

3009 raw_gaze_df = pd.DataFrame() 

3010 else: 

3011 _stash_active_mapping("raw_gaze", raw_gaze_schema) 

3012 raw_gaze_df = normalize_raw_gaze(raw_gaze_df, raw_gaze_schema) 

3013 

3014 return raw_gaze_df 

3015 

3016 

3017# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

3018# Data-source resolution + the panels the top menu bar hosts 

3019# 

3020# `_sidebar_group` is gone with the sidebar: each former group is now its own 

3021# popover on the menu bar (see `menu.render_top_menu`), and the popover's trigger 

3022# label is the group heading. Nothing left to title. 

3023# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- 

3024 

3025 

3026def render_sidebar_data_source(host=None) -> str: 

3027 """Resolve the active data source (renders no picker widget — UX-25). 

3028 

3029 Returns the selected source: ``DEMO_CHOICE`` ("Bundled Demo"), a stored 

3030 uploaded dataset's name, ``ONESTOP_CHOICE`` / ``PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE`` when 

3031 available, ``SYNTHETIC_CHOICE`` if already selected, or ``UPLOAD_CHOICE`` 

3032 while the "➕ Add data" wizard is active. Switching to a stored dataset reloads 

3033 it from session (no re-upload); the synthetic source is no longer offered 

3034 fresh and "Public Datasets" shows grayed-out until the feature flag is on. 

3035 

3036 **UX-25** moved the *visible* picker out of the sidebar and onto the main 

3037 view's "Filter by" row (:func:`render_data_source_picker`). The picker has to 

3038 render inside the tab, i.e. long after the data is loaded, so this function 

3039 keeps its position at the top of ``main`` and stays the resolver: it applies 

3040 the pre-widget ``_pending_source_choice`` seam, heals a stale selection, and 

3041 publishes the entry list the picker renders from (``_data_source_entries``). 

3042 ``data_source_choice`` remains the canonical key (``?source=…`` deep links and 

3043 the wizard's finalize / cancel path both write it). 

3044 

3045 ``host`` is the Data page's *Data source* slot (DATA-26). The one thing this 

3046 function *does* render — the wizard's "✕ Cancel" bar, which stands in for the 

3047 picker while an upload is being added — goes there, so it takes the picker's 

3048 place on the page rather than appearing above it in the bare main area. 

3049 """ 

3050 # Apply a programmatic source switch (the wizard's finalize / Cancel, or the 

3051 # main-view picker's on_change) BEFORE anything reads data_source_choice. It 

3052 # rides a plain key, not a widget value, so the browser never reconciles it 

3053 # away — assigning data_source_choice inline and rerunning is unreliable 

3054 # because the widget's frontend value can overwrite it on the rerun (works in 

3055 # AppTest, not in a real browser). Callbacks run before the script body, so a 

3056 # pick made in the tab still takes effect on the very next run. 

3057 pending = st.session_state.pop("_pending_source_choice", None) 

3058 if pending is not None: 

3059 st.session_state["data_source_choice"] = pending 

3060 # A real source was chosen (finalize / cancel) → leave the wizard. 

3061 st.session_state["_show_upload_wizard"] = False 

3062 

3063 # The upload wizard is tracked by a plain flag, not by parking UPLOAD_CHOICE 

3064 # in the radio key (which Streamlit would garbage-collect mid-wizard — see 

3065 # _enter_add_data_wizard). The legacy ``data_source_choice == UPLOAD_CHOICE`` 

3066 # is still honoured so AppTests / `?source=upload` deep links can open the 

3067 # wizard directly. While it's open the wizard owns the page (the "Filter by" 

3068 # row never renders), so the way out is rendered here, at the top of it. 

3069 if ( 

3070 st.session_state.get("_show_upload_wizard") 

3071 or st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") == UPLOAD_CHOICE 

3072 ): 

3073 # UX-66: the caption is gone (the sticky bar's title says where you are) 

3074 # and ✕ Cancel rides that bar — `wizard._render_data_setup` reserves the 

3075 # slot, and the wizard renders *after* this, so on the very first run of 

3076 # a fresh wizard the slot does not exist yet and it falls back to here. 

3077 # UX-66: ✕ Cancel moved onto the wizard's sticky bar, which is the one 

3078 # row that stays on screen — the way out used to scroll away with the 

3079 # page. It is rendered by `wizard._render_data_setup` via 

3080 # `leave_add_data_wizard` below; nothing is drawn here, because this 

3081 # function runs *before* the wizard and a container reserved now would 

3082 # belong to the previous run. 

3083 return UPLOAD_CHOICE 

3084 

3085 # DATA-9: one **flat** source picker. Every source is a single entry tagged by 

3086 # kind — 🧪 demo · 🔒 private (your uploads + local env bundles) · 🌐 public — 

3087 # instead of a "Public datasets" category that then needed a second selectbox. 

3088 # `data_source_choice` stays the canonical key, but for a public corpus the 

3089 # entry's token IS the registry label; the return value resolves it back to 

3090 # PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE (+ public_dataset_choice) so the load path is unchanged. 

3091 uploaded = list(st.session_state.get("_datasets", {}).keys()) 

3092 entries: list[str] = [] 

3093 kinds: dict[str, str] = {} 

3094 if onestop_data_dir() is not None: 

3095 entries.append(ONESTOP_CHOICE) 

3096 kinds[ONESTOP_CHOICE] = "🔒" 

3097 if multipleye_bundle_dir() is not None: 

3098 entries.append(MULTIPLEYE_BUNDLE_CHOICE) 

3099 kinds[MULTIPLEYE_BUNDLE_CHOICE] = "🔒" 

3100 entries.append(DEMO_CHOICE) 

3101 kinds[DEMO_CHOICE] = "🧪" 

3102 entries.append(AUTHOR_CHOICE) 

3103 kinds[AUTHOR_CHOICE] = "✏️" 

3104 for name in uploaded: 

3105 entries.append(name) 

3106 kinds[name] = "🔒" 

3107 # DATA-27 (Task 11R): every prepared benchmark corpus is in here as its own 

3108 # 🌐 entry, exactly like the built-ins — `public_dataset_registry()` composes 

3109 # the two. Resolved once and reused below so the whole run agrees on one 

3110 # snapshot of a registry that depends on a directory the user can change. 

3111 registry = public_dataset_registry() if public_datasets_enabled() else {} 

3112 for label in registry: 

3113 entries.append(label) 

3114 kinds[label] = "🌐" 

3115 # UX-37: the ground-truth trial is offered **while debug mode is on** (the 

3116 # ❓ Help toggle), rather than only via `?source=synthetic` — a URL the About 

3117 # note and the docs had to spell out, which is the hidden-behind-a-param 

3118 # problem this item exists to remove. It is a six-word verification fixture, 

3119 # not a corpus, so it sits with the other developer affordances instead of 

3120 # in every user's source list. Still selectable when something already chose 

3121 # it, so a `?source=synthetic` link and the AppTests keep working. 

3122 if ( 

3123 debug_enabled() 

3124 or st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") == SYNTHETIC_CHOICE 

3125 ): 

3126 entries.append(SYNTHETIC_CHOICE) 

3127 kinds[SYNTHETIC_CHOICE] = "🧪" 

3128 

3129 # Removing an app-owned/public source means removing it from this session's 

3130 # available list, not deleting packaged files or a public corpus. Keep the 

3131 # stable token intact for links and loader dispatch; the ordinary stale- 

3132 # selection healing below moves away from a source that was just hidden. 

3133 hidden = set(st.session_state.get(HIDDEN_DATASETS_KEY) or []) 

3134 entries = [token for token in entries if token not in hidden] 

3135 kinds = {token: kind for token, kind in kinds.items() if token in entries} 

3136 if not entries: 

3137 # Never strand the app without a loadable source. This can only happen 

3138 # after the user has removed every row one by one in the same session. 

3139 hidden.discard(DEMO_CHOICE) 

3140 st.session_state[HIDDEN_DATASETS_KEY] = sorted(hidden) 

3141 entries = [DEMO_CHOICE] 

3142 kinds = {DEMO_CHOICE: "🧪"} 

3143 

3144 # Migrate a legacy `PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE` selection (old saved state / deep 

3145 # link / the former category radio) to the concrete corpus token so it lands on 

3146 # the right entry. Falls back to the first public corpus (not the demo) when no 

3147 # corpus was remembered, preserving the old "Public datasets → first corpus". 

3148 if st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") == PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE: 

3149 corpus = st.session_state.get("public_dataset_choice") 

3150 if corpus not in registry: 

3151 corpus = next(iter(registry), None) 

3152 st.session_state["data_source_choice"] = corpus or entries[0] 

3153 

3154 # Heal a stale/invalid selection (e.g. a removed dataset) so the picker never 

3155 # errors on an option that is no longer in the list. Anything that *was* a 

3156 # benchmark entry gets its own landing, in preference to `entries[0]` (the 

3157 # demo): the bootstrap placeholder disappears precisely *because* it 

3158 # succeeded, so sending the user who just supplied a bundle path somewhere 

3159 # else entirely answers them with a non-answer — and, the demo rendering no 

3160 # directory input, drops them straight back out of the corpora they found. 

3161 # The same reasoning covers a stale *corpus* label (the bundle directory was 

3162 # repointed, or that corpus was removed from it): another prepared corpus is 

3163 # a better answer than the demo whenever one is reachable (N2). 

3164 stale = str(st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") or "") 

3165 if stale not in entries: 

3166 was_benchmark = stale == BENCHMARK_SETUP_CHOICE or stale.endswith( 

3167 BENCHMARK_LABEL_SUFFIX 

3168 ) 

3169 healed = "" 

3170 if was_benchmark: 

3171 healed = next( 

3172 ( 

3173 label 

3174 for label, spec in registry.items() 

3175 if spec.get("benchmark_dataset") 

3176 ), 

3177 "", 

3178 ) 

3179 st.session_state["data_source_choice"] = healed or entries[0] 

3180 choice = st.session_state["data_source_choice"] 

3181 

3182 # Publish what the main-view picker renders from. It runs inside the tab, 

3183 # after this; recomputing the list there would duplicate the registry / 

3184 # stored-dataset logic above (and could disagree with the healed selection). 

3185 st.session_state["_data_source_entries"] = entries 

3186 st.session_state["_data_source_kinds"] = kinds 

3187 st.session_state["_data_source_uploaded"] = uploaded 

3188 

3189 # Resolve a public-corpus token back to the canonical PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE so 

3190 # every downstream consumer (load dispatch, monitor, filter/col-map reset keys) 

3191 # is unchanged; the chosen corpus rides public_dataset_choice as before. 

3192 if choice in registry: 

3193 st.session_state["public_dataset_choice"] = choice 

3194 return PUBLIC_DATASETS_CHOICE 

3195 return choice 

3196 

3197 

3198def _on_data_source_pick() -> None: 

3199 """Route the main-view picker's choice through the pre-widget seam (UX-25). 

3200

3203 top of ``main`` — applies the new source on the *same* run that renders it. 

3204 The picker rides its own widget key (``data_source_picker``) rather than 

3205 writing ``data_source_choice`` directly, so a deep link / saved config can 

3206 keep assigning the canonical key without the widget reconciling it away.

3208 picked = st.session_state.get("data_source_picker") 

3209 if picked: 

3210 st.session_state["_pending_source_choice"] = picked

3239def discard_and_leave_wizard() -> None: 

3240 """Abandon the half-built dataset and let the trip finish (BUG-31). 

3241 

3242 :func:`leave_add_data_wizard` restores the source the wizard was opened 

3243 *from*. For a **nav-triggered** prompt nothing here needs to navigate: the 

3244 nav has been sitting on the requested view the whole time the prompt was 

3245 up, so closing the wizard is all it takes for the next run to render it. 

3246 

3247 **BUG-36 follow-up:** that assumption breaks for ✕ Cancel, whose prompt 

3248 always names 🗂️ Data as the destination regardless of where the nav 

3249 actually is — click Session, click Keep setting up, then Cancel, and the 

3250 nav is still genuinely on Session throughout; closing the wizard alone 

3251 left it there instead of on Data as promised. Requesting the recorded 

3252 destination through the same ``main_nav`` seam :func:`url_state._go_data` 

3253 and friends use is a no-op for the nav-triggered case (the router is 

3254 already sitting on it, so this just re-affirms the same value) and is 

3255 what actually moves it for Cancel's fixed one. 

3256 """ 

3257 destination = st.session_state.pop(WIZARD_LEAVE_KEY, None) 

3258 st.session_state.pop(WIZARD_STAY_KEY, None) 

3259 leave_add_data_wizard() 

3260 if destination: 

3261 st.session_state["main_nav"] = destination

3264def render_data_source_picker(host=None) -> None: 

3265 """Render the data-source picker in the main view (UX-25). 

3266 

3267 Sits on the "Filter by" row, left of the label, so the top of the page reads 

3268 left-to-right as *which dataset → how to narrow it → which trial* — the app is 

3269 built to be used with the sidebar closed. Renders from the entry list 

3270 :func:`render_sidebar_data_source` published earlier this run; a pick is 

3271 applied on the next run via :func:`_on_data_source_pick`. 

3272 

3273 UX-64 reduced it to the selectbox alone. Adding a dataset, removing one and 

3274 the contribute link were behind a ➕ popover here; the 🗂️ Data page owns all 

3275 three now, and the width it frees is what lets the dataset picker keep its 

3276 size on the single control line. 

3277 """ 

3278 entries = list(st.session_state.get("_data_source_entries") or []) 

3279 if not entries: 

3280 return 

3281 kinds: dict[str, str] = dict(st.session_state.get("_data_source_kinds") or {}) 

3282 uploaded = list(st.session_state.get("_data_source_uploaded") or []) 

3283 

3284 registry = public_dataset_registry() 

3285 

3286 def _entry_label(token: str) -> str: 

3287 # Reads the `registry` snapshot resolved just above rather than calling 

3288 # `public_dataset_registry()` per token: discovery depends on a directory 

3289 # the user can change, so one run must format its options against one 

3290 # snapshot (which is also why the old `_public_dataset_label` helper, 

3291 # which built its own, had no business being called from here — M6). 

3292 tag = kinds.get(token, "") 

3293 if token in registry: 

3294 # `picker_name_for` is the single definition of what this list shows 

3295 # — the entry's `short` plus, while DATA-27 is unfinished on main, a 

3296 # (WIP) marker. Formatting only: the entry's key, its `short` and 

3297 # its share slug are untouched, so dropping the marker later 

3298 # invalidates no link and no saved config. Anything that tells the 

3299 # user to "select X" reads it too, so the two cannot drift. The 

3300 # snapshot is passed in for the M6 reason above it. 

3301 name = _dataset_display_name(token, registry) 

3302 elif token in uploaded: 

3303 name = f"{_dataset_display_name(token, registry)} (yours)" 

3304 else: 

3305 name = _dataset_display_name(token, registry) 

3306 return f"{tag} {name}".strip() 

3307 

3308 # Keyed wrapper → stable `.st-key-…` selector for the spotlight tour. 

3309 box = (host if host is not None else st).container(key="tour_grp_data_source") 

3310 # UX-64: the picker is the whole control now. The ➕ popover that sat beside 

3311 # it — Add data, remove-an-upload, the contribute link — is gone: the 🗂️ Data 

3312 # page is the only way to add a dataset, which is where the wizard renders 

3313 # anyway, and removing one moves there too (#UX-54's dataset table). Dropping 

3314 # it is also what frees the width for the single control line, since the 

3315 # dataset picker itself must **not** shrink — you may be comparing two. 

3316 # 

3317 # Mirror the canonical key onto the widget key before it instantiates, so a 

3318 # deep link / restore / wizard finalize shows up in the picker. 

3319 current = st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") 

3320 if current in entries: 

3321 st.session_state["data_source_picker"] = current 

3322 box.selectbox( 

3323 "**Select Dataset**", 

3324 entries, 

3325 format_func=_entry_label, 

3326 help=( 

3327 "Which dataset the app is showing. Add, rename or remove one on " 

3328 "the 🗂️ Data page." 

3329 ), 

3330 key="data_source_picker", 

3331 on_change=_on_data_source_pick, 

3332 ) 

3333 

3334 

3335#: Cell text of the dataset table's action buttons. `st.column_config.ButtonColumn` 

3336#: takes each button's label from the cell *value*, which is what lets a row that 

3337#: cannot be edited or deleted (a built-in corpus) simply carry no label — and, 

3338#: since UX-78, what lets the **Dataset** column be both the name and the control 

3339#: that opens it. 

3340_DATASET_EDIT_LABEL = ":material/edit: Edit" 

3341_DATASET_RENAME_LABEL = ":material/drive_file_rename_outline: Rename" 

3342_DATASET_REMOVE_LABEL = ":material/delete: Remove" 

3343_DATASET_ABOUT_LABEL = ":material/info: About" 

3344 

3345# Built-in and public dataset tokens are load-path identifiers, so changing 

3346# them would break deep links and loader dispatch. Their table rename is a 

3347# display alias; removing one hides it from this browser session. Uploaded 

3348# datasets keep using the real store re-key/delete operations in `wizard.py`. 

3349DATASET_ALIASES_KEY = "_dataset_display_aliases" 

3350HIDDEN_DATASETS_KEY = "_hidden_dataset_tokens" 

3351PENDING_RENAME_KEY = "_dataset_pending_rename" 

3352#: DATA-35 — the row whose ℹ️ About dialog is open. Same arm-then-read shape as 

3353#: the rename and delete flags above: a table callback sets it, the next run 

3354#: opens the dialog. 

3355PENDING_ABOUT_KEY = "_dataset_pending_about" 

3356 

3357#: UX-78 — the open dataset's row tint. A Styler writes inline CSS and so cannot 

3358#: read the theme's variables; a translucent blue reads as "selected" on both the 

3359#: light and the dark grid without being opaque enough to fight the text. 

3360_DATASET_ACTIVE_TINT = "rgba(59, 130, 246, 0.18)"

3363def _dataset_display_name(token: str, registry: dict | None = None) -> str: 

3364 """User-facing dataset name without changing the source's stable token.""" 

3365 alias = (st.session_state.get(DATASET_ALIASES_KEY) or {}).get(token) 

3366 if alias: 

3367 return str(alias) 

3368 registry = public_dataset_registry() if registry is None else registry 

3369 return picker_name_for(token, registry) if token in registry else token

3371 

3372def _counts_store() -> dict: 

3373 store = st.session_state.get(DATASET_COUNTS_STORE_KEY) 

3374 if not isinstance(store, dict): 

3375 store = {} 

3376 st.session_state[DATASET_COUNTS_STORE_KEY] = store 

3377 return store 

3378 

3379 

3380def remembered_dataset_counts( 

3381 token: str, 

3382 words: pd.DataFrame | None, 

3383 fixations: pd.DataFrame | None, 

3384 raw_gaze: pd.DataFrame | None = None, 

3385) -> dict: 

3386 """This dataset's headline counts, computed at most once per version of it. 

3387 

3388 **DATA-32.** Three cases, in order: 

3389 

3390 1. **Frames in memory** (the open dataset, and every stored upload) — the 

3391 counts are keyed on the frames' fingerprints, so a remembered entry is 

3392 reused only while it still describes *these* rows. A remap, a re-upload 

3393 or any other edit changes the fingerprint and the counts are recomputed; 

3394 staleness is therefore not possible, which is what makes remembering them 

3395 safe at all. 

3396 2. **Frames not loaded, but counted before** — the remembered row is shown. 

3397 This is the case the item is for: a public corpus you opened last week no 

3398 longer costs minutes to list. 

3399 3. **Never counted** — blank, as before. Nothing is read from disk to fill a 

3400 table. 

3401 

3402 The store is pruned by :func:`forget_dataset_counts` when a dataset leaves 

3403 the session, and cleared with the recovery cache. 

3404 """ 

3405 store = _counts_store() 

3406 entry = store.get(token) 

3407 if words is None and fixations is None and raw_gaze is None: 

3408 counts = entry.get("counts") if isinstance(entry, dict) else None 

3409 remembered = dict(counts) if isinstance(counts, dict) else {} 

3410 # Recovery manifests written before this table matched the inspection 

3411 # summary called the same value Readers. Preserve it without loading the 

3412 # dataset merely to refresh a label. 

3413 if "Participants" not in remembered and "Readers" in remembered: 

3414 remembered["Participants"] = remembered.pop("Readers") 

3415 return remembered 

3416 key = [ 

3417 frame_fingerprint(words), 

3418 frame_fingerprint(fixations), 

3419 frame_fingerprint(raw_gaze), 

3420 ] 

3421 if isinstance(entry, dict) and entry.get("key") == key: 

3422 return dict(entry.get("counts") or {}) 

3423 counts = _dataset_counts(words, fixations, raw_gaze, tuple(key)) 

3424 store[token] = {"key": key, "counts": dict(counts)} 

3425 return dict(counts) 

3426 

3427 

3428def forget_dataset_counts(keep: set | None = None) -> None: 

3429 """Drop remembered counts for datasets that are no longer listed (DATA-32). 

3430 

3431 ``keep=None`` forgets all of them — used by recovery-cache clearing and by 

3432 the dataset-removal cache invalidation path. 

3433 """ 

3434 store = _counts_store() 

3435 for token in [t for t in store if keep is None or t not in keep]: 

3436 store.pop(token, None) 

3437 

3438 

3439@st.cache_data(show_spinner=False) 

3440def _dataset_counts( 

3441 _words: pd.DataFrame, 

3442 _fixations: pd.DataFrame, 

3443 _raw_gaze: pd.DataFrame, 

3444 key, 

3445) -> dict: 

3446 """Cheap headline counts for every field in the dataset summary row. 

3447 

3448 Two ``nunique`` calls and two lengths — UX-54 asked for "measurements that 

3449 are easy to calculate", and anything needing the measures pipeline would make 

3450 *listing* the datasets as expensive as opening them. Cached on the frames' 

3451 fingerprints (``key``), since this runs for every listed dataset on every 

3452 rerun of the page. 

3453 

3454 **``key`` has no leading underscore, and that is the whole point.** 

3455 ``@st.cache_data`` skips underscore-prefixed arguments when it builds its 

3456 cache key — that is how the frames are passed without being hashed — so the 

3457 fingerprint argument was being skipped too (DATA-32 found it): the cache had 

3458 exactly *one* entry, and every dataset after the first was served the first 

3459 one's counts. UX-54 r2 had hidden it by counting only the open dataset. 

3460 """ 

3461 

3462 def _n_unique(frame, column): 

3463 if frame is None or frame.empty or column not in frame.columns: 

3464 return None 

3465 return int(frame[column].nunique()) 

3466 

3467 words = _words if _words is not None else pd.DataFrame() 

3468 fixations = _fixations if _fixations is not None else pd.DataFrame() 

3469 raw_gaze = _raw_gaze if _raw_gaze is not None else pd.DataFrame() 

3470 frames = (fixations, words, raw_gaze) 

3471 

3472 def _union_unique(column: str): 

3473 values = set() 

3474 found = False 

3475 for frame in frames: 

3476 if frame is None or frame.empty or column not in frame.columns: 

3477 continue 

3478 found = True 

3479 values.update(frame[column].dropna().astype(str).tolist()) 

3480 return len(values) if found else None 

3481 

3482 text_column = "unique_text_id" if "unique_text_id" in words else "text_id" 

3483 screens = len(part_catalog(words, fixations, raw_gaze)) or None 

3484 return { 

3485 "Participants": _union_unique("participant_id"), 

3486 "Texts": _n_unique(words, text_column), 

3487 "Trials": _union_unique("trial_id"), 

3488 "Screens": screens, 

3489 "Words": len(words) or None, 

3490 "Fixations": len(fixations) or None, 

3491 "Gaze points": len(raw_gaze) or None, 

3492 } 

3493 

3494

3499 wizard finalize use: ``data_source_choice`` is a widget key elsewhere, so 

3500 this is the one way an assignment lands before the widgets instantiate. 

3501 """ 

3502 st.session_state["_pending_source_choice"] = name 

3503 st.session_state["data_source_choice"] = name

3509PENDING_DELETE_KEY = "_dataset_pending_delete"

3512@st.dialog("Remove this dataset?") 

3513def _delete_confirmation_dialog( 

3514 token: str, *, uploaded: set[str], available: list[str] 

3515) -> None: 

3516 """The modal body — UX-79. Opened by ``_render_delete_confirmation``. 

3517 

3518 **BUG-36:** handled by the button's *return value*, not ``on_click`` — an 

3519 ``st.dialog`` body is a fragment, so an ``on_click`` callback here reran 

3520 only the dialog: the deletion happened, but ``main()`` never re-executed, 

3521 so the modal sat there looking inert. ``st.rerun(scope="app")`` both closes 

3522 the modal and re-renders the page underneath (see ``tour.py``'s 

3523 ``_tutorial_library_dialog``, which hit the same trap first). 

3524 """ 

3525 owned = token in uploaded 

3526 if owned: 

3527 st.warning( 

3528 f"Remove **{_dataset_display_name(token)}**? Its tables, column " 

3529 "mapping and annotations leave this session — there is no undo." 

3530 ) 

3531 else: 

3532 st.caption( 

3533 f"Remove **{_dataset_display_name(token)}** from Available datasets " 

3534 "for this session? The packaged or public source data is not deleted." 

3535 ) 

3536 remaining = [entry for entry in available if entry != token] 

3537 yes, no = st.columns(2) 

3538 if yes.button( 

3539 "Remove", 

3540 key="dataset_delete_confirm", 

3541 type="primary", 

3542 width="stretch", 

3543 disabled=not remaining, 

3544 ): 

3545 pending = st.session_state.pop(PENDING_DELETE_KEY, None) 

3546 if owned: 

3547 # Local import, like `_enter_add_data_wizard` above: `wizard` 

3548 # imports `app` back, so it cannot be imported at module load. 

3549 from scanpath_studio.wizard import _remove_dataset 

3550 

3551 _remove_dataset(pending) 

3552 else: 

3553 hidden = set(st.session_state.get(HIDDEN_DATASETS_KEY) or []) 

3554 hidden.add(pending) 

3555 st.session_state[HIDDEN_DATASETS_KEY] = sorted(hidden) 

3556 if st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") == pending: 

3557 st.session_state["_pending_source_choice"] = remaining[0] 

3558 st.rerun(scope="app") 

3559 if not remaining: 

3560 st.caption("At least one dataset must remain available.") 

3561 if no.button( 

3562 "Keep it", 

3563 key="dataset_delete_cancel", 

3564 width="stretch", 

3565 ): 

3566 st.session_state.pop(PENDING_DELETE_KEY, None) 

3567 st.rerun(scope="app")

3570def _render_delete_confirmation(host, tokens: list, uploaded: set[str]) -> None: 

3571 """The confirm step between ✕ Delete and the dataset actually going away. 

3572 

3573 Deleting an upload drops its frames, its mapping and its annotations from 

3574 the session with no undo, and the button that starts it is one cell away 

3575 from ✏️ Edit in a table row — so the click arms this, and this asks. 

3576 

3577 **UX-79** made it a modal rather than a block under the table: the question 

3578 is raised by a click *in* the table, and on a long list of datasets a 

3579 container below it can be off-screen from the row that asked. The arming 

3580 flag is unchanged — a dialog is opened by calling it, so what moved is where 

3581 the flag is read. A token that has since disappeared (the dataset was 

3582 removed another way) disarms itself instead of opening a dialog about 

3583 nothing. 

3584 """ 

3585 token = st.session_state.get(PENDING_DELETE_KEY) 

3586 if token is None: 

3587 return 

3588 if token not in tokens: 

3589 st.session_state.pop(PENDING_DELETE_KEY, None) 

3590 return 

3591 _delete_confirmation_dialog(token, uploaded=uploaded, available=tokens) 

3592

3594def _unique_dataset_alias(requested: str, token: str, tokens: list[str]) -> str: 

3595 """A non-empty display name that does not duplicate another table row.""" 

3596 base = requested.strip() or _dataset_display_name(token) 

3597 used = { 

3598 _dataset_display_name(other).casefold() for other in tokens if other != token 

3599 } 

3600 candidate = base 

3601 suffix = 2 

3602 while candidate.casefold() in used: 

3603 candidate = f"{base} ({suffix})" 

3604 suffix += 1 

3605 return candidate

3709 Deliberately the add-dataset screen's bar, down to the CSS class: the ask 

3710 was that "the Add Dataset and Edit Dataset screens should be very similar", 

3711 and the two screens ask the same questions of the same dataset — one before 

3712 it exists and one after. The difference is the title (this one names the 

3713 dataset) and the way out, which here is a return rather than a cancel: an 

3714 edit is applied by its own section's button, so leaving discards nothing and 

3715 needs no confirmation. 

3716 """ 

3717 name = _dataset_display_name( 

3718 str(st.session_state.get("data_source_choice") or data_choice) 

3719 ) 

3720 bar = host.container(key="dataset_editor_bar") 

3721 title_col, back_col = bar.columns([8, 2], vertical_alignment="center") 

3722 title_col.markdown( 

3723 f'<div class="sps-wiz-title">✏️ Edit {html.escape(name)}</div>', 

3724 unsafe_allow_html=True, 

3725 ) 

3726 back_col.button( 

3727 "← Back to datasets", 

3728 key="dataset_editor_close", 

3729 on_click=_close_dataset_editor, 

3730 width="stretch", 

3731 help="Return to 📂 Available datasets. Changes you have already applied " 

3732 "are kept.", 

3733 ) 

3734 bar.caption( 

3735 "How this dataset is read and measured — where its files are, how its " 

3736 "columns map onto the app's fields, the screen it was recorded on, and " 

3737 "any metadata tables attached to it. The same questions the " 

3738 "add-dataset screen asks, for a dataset that already exists." 

3739 ) 

3740 

3741 

3742#: DATA-35 — set by a row action that genuinely changes what the app is showing 

3743#: (opening a dataset, opening the editor), read at the top of the table 

3744#: fragment. A widget callback may not call ``st.rerun``, and a *fragment* rerun 

3745#: would redraw the table alone while the page under it still showed the old 

3746#: dataset — so the callback asks and the fragment body does it. 

3747_TABLE_NEEDS_APP_RERUN = "_dataset_table_needs_app_rerun" 

3748 

3749 

3750@st.fragment 

3751def render_dataset_table( 

3752 host=None, 

3753 *, 

3754 active: str | None = None, 

3755 words: pd.DataFrame | None = None, 

3756 fixations: pd.DataFrame | None = None, 

3757 raw_gaze: pd.DataFrame | None = None, 

3758) -> None: 

3759 """The 🗂️ Data page's dataset list, as a table (UX-54). 

3760 

3761 One row per dataset — the same entries the picker offers — carrying the 

3762 full summary counts and the actions belonging to that dataset: **Open** it, 

3763 **Edit** its column mapping, **Rename** it, or **Remove** it. Sortable and 

3764 scrollable by virtue of being an ``st.dataframe``, which is what a column of 

3765 cards could not be. 

3766 

3767 **Counts are only shown for data already in memory** — the open dataset 

3768 (whose frames are passed in) and every stored upload. A public corpus is not 

3769 read until it is opened, and loading eight of them to fill a table would cost 

3770 minutes; those rows stay blank. 

3771 

3772 Args: 

3773 host: Container to render into. Defaults to the page. 

3774 active: The open dataset's entry token, marked in the table. 

3775 words: The open dataset's word frame, for its counts. 

3776 fixations: Its fixation frame. 

3777 """ 

3778 # DATA-35: a row action that only opens a dialog — About, Rename, Remove — 

3779 # costs a *fragment* rerun, not a whole-app one. Renaming a dataset used to 

3780 # take two full page renders (one to open the modal, one to apply it) on a 

3781 # page that draws a forty-row table, the whole column mapping and three 

3782 # upload widgets; the first of those is now this box redrawing itself. 

3783 if st.session_state.pop(_TABLE_NEEDS_APP_RERUN, False): 

3784 st.rerun(scope="app") 

3785 entries = list(st.session_state.get("_data_source_entries") or []) 

3786 if not entries: 

3787 return 

3788 kinds = dict(st.session_state.get("_data_source_kinds") or {}) 

3789 uploaded = set(st.session_state.get("_data_source_uploaded") or []) 

3790 stored_uploads = dict(st.session_state.get("_datasets") or {}) 

3791 registry = public_dataset_registry() 

3792 # DATA-32: a dataset that has left the list takes its remembered counts with 

3793 # it — deleted, renamed, or a public corpus whose location was unset. 

3794 forget_dataset_counts(keep={t for t in entries if t != UPLOAD_CHOICE}) 

3795 

3796 kind_labels = { 

3797 "🧪": "Demo", 

3798 "✏️": "Manual", 

3799 "🔒": "Private", 

3800 "🌐": "Public", 

3801 } 

3802 rows = [] 

3803 for token in entries: 

3804 if token == UPLOAD_CHOICE: 

3805 continue # the wizard, not a dataset 

3806 own = token in uploaded 

3807 name = _dataset_display_name(token, registry) 

3808 # DATA-32: counted once per version of a dataset and remembered, so a 

3809 # row keeps its numbers without the frames being in memory. UX-54 r2 had 

3810 # narrowed this to the open dataset because counting meant *loading*; 

3811 # with a store that argument only applies to a corpus nobody has opened 

3812 # yet, and those rows are still blank rather than guessed at. 

3813 if token == active: 

3814 frames = (words, fixations, raw_gaze) 

3815 elif token in stored_uploads: 

3816 entry = stored_uploads.get(token) or {} 

3817 frames = ( 

3818 entry.get("words"), 

3819 entry.get("fixations"), 

3820 entry.get("raw_gaze"), 

3821 ) 

3822 else: 

3823 frames = (None, None, None) 

3824 counts = remembered_dataset_counts(token, *frames) 

3825 about = dataset_about(token, registry) 

3826 rows.append( 

3827 { 

3828 # UX-78: the name *is* the button. `ButtonColumn` takes its label 

3829 # from the cell value, so the column that says which dataset a 

3830 # row is can also be the control that opens it — which retires 

3831 # both the ▶ marker column and the separate Open column. The open 

3832 # dataset is the coloured row instead (see the Styler below). 

3833 "Dataset": name, 

3834 "Kind": ( 

3835 f"{kinds[token]} {kind_labels.get(kinds[token], '')}".strip() 

3836 if kinds.get(token) 

3837 else ("🔒 Private" if own else "") 

3838 ), 

3839 # DATA-35: the two facts about a corpus that fit in a cell. The 

3840 # description and the coordinate provenance are sentences, so 

3841 # they live one click away in the ℹ️ About dialog instead. 

3842 "Language": about.get("language") or "", 

3843 "Home": about.get("link") or None, 

3844 "Participants": counts.get("Participants"), 

3845 "Texts": counts.get("Texts"), 

3846 "Trials": counts.get("Trials"), 

3847 "Screens": counts.get("Screens"), 

3848 "Fixations": counts.get("Fixations"), 

3849 "Words": counts.get("Words"), 

3850 "Gaze points": counts.get("Gaze points"), 

3851 "About": _DATASET_ABOUT_LABEL, 

3852 "Edit": _DATASET_EDIT_LABEL, 

3853 "Rename": _DATASET_RENAME_LABEL, 

3854 "Remove": _DATASET_REMOVE_LABEL, 

3855 "_token": token, 

3856 "_active": token == active, 

3857 } 

3858 ) 

3859 if not rows: 

3860 return 

3861 frame = pd.DataFrame(rows) 

3862 tokens = frame.pop("_token").tolist() 

3863 # Missing counts are legitimate for a corpus that has never been opened. 

3864 # Pandas would normally upcast those columns to float (and Streamlit would 

3865 # display e.g. ``24.0``), so keep them as nullable integers explicitly. 

3866 count_columns = [ 

3867 "Participants", 

3868 "Texts", 

3869 "Trials", 

3870 "Screens", 

3871 "Fixations", 

3872 "Words", 

3873 "Gaze points", 

3874 ] 

3875 for column in count_columns: 

3876 frame[column] = pd.array(frame[column], dtype="Int64") 

3877 

3878 def _clicked(state_key): 

3879 """The token of the row whose button was clicked, or ``None``. 

3880 

3881 ``click["row"]`` is a position in the frame handed to ``st.dataframe``, 

3882 not in whatever order the user sorted the columns into — the same 

3883 source-position semantics dataframe selections have — so this parallel 

3884 list stays correct under client-side sorting (the ENG-36 pattern). 

3885 """ 

3886 click = st.session_state.get(state_key) 

3887 row = click["row"] if click else None 

3888 if row is not None and 0 <= row < len(tokens): 

3889 return tokens[row] 

3890 return None 

3891 

3892 def _on_open() -> None: 

3893 # UX-78: raised by a click on the dataset's *name*. 

3894 token = _clicked("dataset_table_name") 

3895 if token is not None: 

3896 _select_dataset(token) 

3897 st.session_state[_TABLE_NEEDS_APP_RERUN] = True 

3898 

3899 def _on_edit() -> None: 

3900 # DATA-35: "a screen similar to add-dataset" is now literally a screen. 

3901 # Edit opens the dataset and raises the ✏️ Edit dataset screen over the 

3902 # overview — the column mapping, the recording setup, the source's 

3903 # options and location, the identity check and the metadata tables are 

3904 # all on it. `FOCUS_MAPPING_KEY` still rides along for the mapping 

3905 # editor's "editing <name>" line. 

3906 token = _clicked("dataset_table_edit") 

3907 if token is not None: 

3908 _select_dataset(token) 

3909 st.session_state[FOCUS_MAPPING_KEY] = token 

3910 st.session_state[DATASET_EDITOR_OPEN_KEY] = True 

3911 st.session_state[_TABLE_NEEDS_APP_RERUN] = True 

3912 

3913 def _on_delete() -> None: 

3914 # UX-54 r2: arm, don't delete. The click lands on a row of a table — one 

3915 # cell away from ✏️ Edit — and an upload is not recoverable from the 

3916 # session once dropped, so the button asks and the confirmation below 

3917 # does the work. 

3918 token = _clicked("dataset_table_delete") 

3919 if token is not None: 

3920 st.session_state[PENDING_DELETE_KEY] = token 

3921 

3922 def _on_rename() -> None: 

3923 token = _clicked("dataset_table_rename") 

3924 if token is not None: 

3925 st.session_state[PENDING_RENAME_KEY] = token 

3926 

3927 def _on_about() -> None: 

3928 token = _clicked("dataset_table_about") 

3929 if token is not None: 

3930 st.session_state[PENDING_ABOUT_KEY] = token 

3931 

3932 box = host if host is not None else st 

3933 # UX-78: the open dataset is a tinted row rather than a ▶ in a column of its 

3934 # own. A Styler is the only per-row colour `st.dataframe` takes, and it is 

3935 # applied to the whole row so the tint reads as "this one" rather than as a 

3936 # highlighted cell. The colour is `color-mix`-free on purpose — a Styler 

3937 # emits inline CSS, which cannot see the theme's variables — so it is a 

3938 # translucent accent that sits legibly on both the light and the dark grid. 

3939 active_row = next((i for i, row in enumerate(rows) if row["_active"]), None) 

3940 frame = frame.drop(columns=["_active"]) 

3941 # A Styler is required for the active-row tint; the underlying nullable 

3942 # integer dtypes remain intact for numeric display and sorting. 

3943 display = frame.style 

3944 if active_row is not None: 

3945 display = display.apply( 

3946 lambda row: ( 

3947 [ 

3948 f"background-color: {_DATASET_ACTIVE_TINT}" 

3949 if row.name == active_row 

3950 else "" 

3951 ] 

3952 * len(row) 

3953 ), 

3954 axis=1, 

3955 ) 

3956 box.dataframe( 

3957 display, 

3958 width="stretch", 

3959 hide_index=True, 

3960 column_config={ 

3961 "Dataset": st.column_config.ButtonColumn( 

3962 "Dataset", 

3963 width="medium", 

3964 type="tertiary", 

3965 help="Open this dataset.", 

3966 on_click=_on_open, 

3967 key="dataset_table_name", 

3968 ), 

3969 "Kind": st.column_config.TextColumn("Kind", width="small"), 

3970 "Language": st.column_config.TextColumn("Language", width="small"), 

3971 "Home": st.column_config.LinkColumn( 

3972 "Home", 

3973 width="small", 

3974 display_text="Open ↗", 

3975 help="The corpus' own home page or repository.", 

3976 ), 

3977 "Participants": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3978 "Participants", width="small", format="%d" 

3979 ), 

3980 "Texts": st.column_config.NumberColumn("Texts", width="small", format="%d"), 

3981 "Trials": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3982 "Trials", width="small", format="%d" 

3983 ), 

3984 "Screens": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3985 "Screens", width="small", format="%d" 

3986 ), 

3987 "Fixations": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3988 "Fixations", width="small", format="%d" 

3989 ), 

3990 "Words": st.column_config.NumberColumn("Words", width="small", format="%d"), 

3991 "Gaze points": st.column_config.NumberColumn( 

3992 "Gaze points", width="small", format="%d" 

3993 ), 

3994 "About": st.column_config.ButtonColumn( 

3995 "", 

3996 type="tertiary", 

3997 width="small", 

3998 help="What this dataset is, and where its coordinates come from.", 

3999 on_click=_on_about, 

4000 key="dataset_table_about", 

4001 ), 

4002 "Edit": st.column_config.ButtonColumn( 

4003 "", 

4004 type="tertiary", 

4005 width="small", 

4006 help="Open it and edit its column mapping and recording setup.", 

4007 on_click=_on_edit, 

4008 key="dataset_table_edit", 

4009 ), 

4010 "Rename": st.column_config.ButtonColumn( 

4011 "", 

4012 type="tertiary", 

4013 width="small", 

4014 help="Rename this dataset.", 

4015 on_click=_on_rename, 

4016 key="dataset_table_rename", 

4017 ), 

4018 "Remove": st.column_config.ButtonColumn( 

4019 "", 

4020 type="tertiary", 

4021 width="small", 

4022 help="Remove this dataset from the session.", 

4023 on_click=_on_delete, 

4024 key="dataset_table_delete", 

4025 ), 

4026 }, 

4027 ) 

4028 _render_about_dialog(tokens, registry) 

4029 _render_rename_dialog(tokens, uploaded) 

4030 _render_delete_confirmation(box, tokens, uploaded) 

4031 if note := st.session_state.pop("_dataset_table_note", None): 

4032 box.success(note)
